versions.notes: - Blink and talk pictures now ask only for the eye or mouth change, so the model keeps the same bust.

- Now in Download Agents for Engine staging testers.
- Checked against the Engine's live faces and lip sync, and its tools for making blink and talking pictures or a mesh avatar from one of your sprites.

- First release: animated 2D avatars for characters and personas in Roleplay and Game.
- Works with PNGTuber-style sprites (your own expression sprites, with blink and talk pictures) and mesh avatar files.
- Ships the prompts for making blink and talk pictures and a mesh avatar from one of your sprites.

- Now in Download Agents for Engine staging testers.
- Checked against the Engine's live faces and lip sync.

- First release: animated 3D avatars for characters and personas in Roleplay and Game.
- Works with VRM models (versions 0.x and 1.0), with an optional idle animation.
- Clicking elsewhere in the chat no longer closes Beholder when you opened it from its shortcut. It stays open until you close it or leave the chat.
- Closing the first-open note, or picking from the build menu, no longer closes Beholder when you opened it from its shortcut.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.
- Paper-doll slots can be reached by keyboard and opened with Enter or Space. Their focus outline stays visible, and closing the editor returns focus to its slot.

- New Conversation game: play Blackjack against the house with up to six characters, from /blackjack or the games picker.
- Pick a character to deal and call each round in their own voice, or let the house deal silently.
- Hit, stand, double down, and split a pair once. Blackjack pays 3 to 2, and the dealer can hit or stand on soft 17.
- Set the starting chips, minimum bet, decks in the shoe, and an optional round limit.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.
- On compatible Engines, report only changed or removed tracker values while preserving unchanged state and locked rows. Older Engines retain the full-output format.

- When a character changes their status or activity during a call, the change now goes on their character card, as it does after a chat reply, so it shows in every chat and lasts for the time they gave. Before, the call changed only this chat's copy of their schedule, and the change was soon lost. (#1498)

- Opening a call no longer changes the volume of, or mutes, a reply Marinara is reading aloud in another chat. The call's voice volume and mute apply only to the call's own voices.
- A call in a chat that uses the Local Model now answers through Marinara's Local Model, as the chat does. Before, it stayed silent and showed no error.

- Calls now uses Marinara Engine's own settings, dialogs, voice playback, Local Model, Local Whisper, haptics, Spotify and chat saving instead of carrying copies of them. It no longer resets your Engine settings, starts a second Local Model, or overwrites chat changes saved while a call runs. The download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1478, #1487)
- During a call, the connection switcher and the sticker and emoji settings change the call's chat, not another chat.
- On phones, the Chat Settings bubble no longer covers the close button in Call Chat. It hides while Call Chat is open and comes back when you close it. (#1338)

- With a Claude (Subscription) connection, Calls no longer makes a hidden second request to name each session, and a request now stops with an error if Claude Code turns on claude.ai connectors. With a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0, Claude Code also no longer adds your account email, the date or this computer's details to the prompt. Engine 2.5.0's Claude Code still adds them, and the server log warns about it until you update Marinara. (#1313)
- Characters can call you on their own again. With the call command on, a character who decides to call you now rings with an incoming call. Before this, nothing happened.

- Mic recording calls no longer lose some of your speech with "Selected provider/model cannot receive provider-native audio input."
- A call left in a background tab or behind other windows no longer cuts a sentence into pieces at short pauses. It now waits until it has heard about 3 seconds of quiet, so replies there can take a little longer.

- Mic recording calls use your own speech-to-text server when it is turned on in Connections → Speech to Text (newer Engines). Local Whisper still handles speech when the server is off or fails.
- Speech you record while an earlier clip is still being transcribed now waits its turn instead of being dropped.
- Keep calls responsive when Safari blocks voice playback: wait for a new touch or key press, and let stopping a call cancel pending playback.
- SwarmUI video connections now generate character call clips using their saved workflow, resolution, frame rate, and LoRAs. Backup SwarmUI connections keep their own workflow settings.
- Keep required reasoning enabled for GLM 5.3 on NanoGPT and Z.AI when the selected effort is None.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.
- On compatible Engines, report only changed or removed tracker values while preserving unchanged state and locked rows. Older Engines retain the full-output format.
- Maintenance rebuild for the shared expression-image lifecycle. Gacha Forge keeps its existing automatic expression behavior; the explicit repaint controls belong to Otome Hearth.
- Maintenance rebuild for the shared image-reference helper. Gacha Forge keeps its existing avatar and outfit reference behavior.

- Characters can equip their designated weapons even when a saved weapon has a different type from their role. The intended owner sees it in Gear and can equip it without regenerating the weapon. Signature skills still activate only for their owner; other characters keep the normal weapon-type rules.
- On short landscape screens, Gear details keep their full height and the panel scrolls, so Choose and Change remain clickable instead of being clipped inside the card.
- The narrator, the chapter planners and characters writing messages are asked to read every character's mind more carefully: what each one knows, wants and feels.

- Scenes, key images, story event art, chat photos, Bond backgrounds and banners now send each character's face (their card's avatar, your persona's, or their saved portrait) and, when the picture paints them in the outfit they have on, that outfit's image too. A character card's unit used to send only its card avatar.
- Banners and Bond backgrounds now paint a unit in the outfit it has on while **Outfits** is on, as chat photos do. Scenes and key images paint and send it only when **The story uses worn outfits** is on (off by default) and the scene does not dress the character itself.
- Faces go before outfits, at most four images, the Engine's limit: outfits are left out first, and the log says so.
- A new portrait or outfit is painted from the face alone, so the outfit a unit has on no longer leaks into its new look.

- A finished story event's fights now open on **Hard**, then **Very Hard**, while the event runs and Seasonal events is on: Hard once the event is done, Very Hard once every fight is won on Hard, as in a main chapter. They are the fights you played, stronger, at 5 Vigor each, and each win pays once per difficulty what a main chapter's Hard and Very Hard fights pay. No new fight is designed, and each difficulty keeps its own progress.
- In **Chapters** a finished event shows its N, H and V marks, and **Enter event** while its Hard fights are open. **Events → Story events** counts its Hard and Very Hard wins.
- A story event's map no longer lists a chapter's Funds, Aether and rank on Normal, which an event never paid, and a played event's map opens without waiting for a scene being written elsewhere.

- A story event you played now sits in **Chapters** right after the chapter it followed, as a finished Character Story does, instead of in a list below the next chapter. Its card says Done, Ended or Paused (Seasonal events off) and opens it to read its scenes again. Stories after the same chapter appear in the order you opened them. **Events → Story events** offers **Revisit played scenes** for a finished event, not **Continue event**.
- A finished story event's map no longer offers Hard and Very Hard. Events are Normal-only, so those fights could never start, and **Start battle** did nothing. A fight that can't start now says why, with **Retry** and **Back**, in chapters, Character Stories, events, Materials and the Tower, and a cleared event fight is turned away before its briefing.
- **Start battle** no longer stays disabled on a cheaper fight after another was refused for Vigor, and works at once in a world you switched to while a fight was starting.

- Nothing changes in play. Expression portraits, choice labels, dialogue voice picking, music briefs, soundtracks and a few log lines now take optional settings, so another package can reuse them. Gacha Forge keeps its own values for all of them.

- A chapter you forged before starting a story event no longer keeps pre-forging while the event holds it, and a big choice it already wrote no longer stops the event from starting, its scenes or its pre-forge. Once the event is finished, ends or Seasonal events is turned off, **Continue** on the chapter's map picks its pre-forge up again, and its choice waits for you as before. A Character Story's pending choice still stops the event from starting.
- While story memory catches up, a companion chat, a character message or a Character Story knows only the scenes you have played, not the ones pre-forge wrote ahead or a Compress summary of them.

- **Chapters → What happens next** can offer the season's story event beside the next chapter and any Character Story, when the next chapter is not forged yet; otherwise **Events → Story events** starts it as before. It starts like a Character Story: its map opens and the next chapter waits. While it is open, its card takes the chapter's place.
- Pre-forge now writes story events too: scenes ahead at no Vigor cost, each fight designed after the scene before it, art in **Story and images**, and the pre-forge bar with Cancel on the event's map. Written scenes can be played while the rest is written. It stops once the event ends.

- Backing out of a fight while it loads and entering another now loads the new fight, not the one you left. A fight request that never answers no longer blocks later fights.
- In Formation, a swap seats both units before either one's passive fires, so a revive, Swap, Shuffle or Echo it sets off never puts a fourth unit in a row, and revived units are drawn where they are. Fights started earlier keep their rules.
- On a small model, replies are much less likely to fail while memory catches up: the oldest chapter summaries, or the oldest chapters of the full story history, are left out only when the reply would not fit otherwise. The previous chapter, the scene so far and your decisions always stay.
- Story memory no longer stops for good when a chapter it already remembers reads differently later: it keeps its first memory and goes on.
- Seasonal event fights load again after a chapter was regenerated, and a fight that can't be set up now says why.

- Scenes that are already written can be played while pre-forge writes the rest of the chapter. Cleared scenes keep **Read again**, and a fight or a written scene you have reached keeps **Play** or **Start**. Only a scene that is not written yet waits for pre-forge, which writes it at no Vigor cost. Back on the chapter map, it turns into Play as soon as it is written.
- Opening a weapon's page from Gear, or a relic's **Upgrade**, keeps the current view until the new one has loaded instead of cutting to an empty screen, and the relic you are upgrading is no longer faded out.

- Story memory recalls by meaning as well as by words, using the Engine's embedding model when one is set, and searches with what was just played or said instead of the chapter plan. Only clearly relevant memories come back: up to three chapter summaries and three side memories.
- A unit's chats stay private. They are no longer folded into the shared overview, and never reach another unit's chat, a scene or event without that unit, or a fight.
- Characters in scenes and chats know only what they saw, took part in or were told in the story, and nothing outside it.

- A seasonal story event can start right after you finish a chapter again. Only a story you are in the middle of keeps an event closed: a main chapter or Character Story part with some, but not all, of it played. One you forged but have not started yet no longer blocks it, and waits until the event is done.
- The event card now says what to finish first ("Finish Chapter 3" or "Finish Arden's Character Story"), and starting a chapter while an event is open names the event to finish.

- A new chapter opens as soon as its plan is written. Its fights are no longer all designed before the chapter map appears: each fight is designed in the background right after the scene before it is written (by pre-forge or when you open it), so it is ready, with its enemy art, when you reach it.
- Story memory summarizes only in the background, so writing a plan, scene, fight or chat no longer waits for it to catch up. Canon the saved overview does not cover yet is sent beside it as its summary, or as written for a fresh side story or chat. A summary already running on the same connection still finishes first; a separate summary connection avoids that.
- Long chapters can be summarized again: summaries get at least 10k tokens of output room for thinking models (or the model's maximum, never below 8,192).

- In character chats, Enter now adds a new line instead of sending. Only **Send** sends your message, so a stray Enter can no longer send it early.
- Auto in story scenes no longer turns itself off when background work starts or finishes, such as expression portraits, scenes written ahead or portraits painting, or when you switch tabs and come back. The current line's voice no longer replays either.
- While a story is written in the background, Formation changes stick: a picked unit, a drag or the bench scroll are no longer reset mid-move, saves never land out of order, and a battle waits for your last change. The chapter map no longer redraws every few seconds, and background writing no longer stalls other screens.

- New **Expression portraits** setting in World → Sources → Images, off by default. Story portraits then show anger, fear, sadness or joy line by line, marked in the same request that writes the scene. Four faces per look are painted in the background, only for characters who speak. A failed set is not retried on its own: turn the setting off and on to try once more.
- Your persona keeps its own voice even when another character shares part of its name, and turning Voice other characters off and on again no longer asks to pay again for combat lines that were never made.

- New **Voice other characters** toggle next to Read character dialogue. NPCs and units without an assigned voice speak with a voice from the Engine's Random NPC Voices lists (Connections → Text to Speech), matched to male or female when known. With both lists empty, any voice of the current connection is used. Each name keeps the same voice. Assigned voices still win, and your persona uses only its own.
- Combat voice lines now play in Classic and Formation fights, start preparing when the battle screen opens, and include your persona's assigned voice. A short notice says when nobody in the team can be voiced.

- When a Front Row unit falls in Formation, a Back Row unit on its side steps into the empty seat at once and acts from its next turn. This works for your team and for enemies, and a fight now ends only when one side has nobody left. Moving and retreating never pull a support forward. A fight started before this update is still scored by the rules it was played under.
- Messages you send in character chats are no longer read aloud. Your persona's assigned voice still reads its story dialogue.

- Require the Engine version that supplies agent reference lorebooks, so an older Engine with a different capability update cannot accept an incompatible World Maps package. Update both the Engine and World Maps together.

- World Maps can use the reference lorebook selected for it in Chat Settings. Matching entries help chat-specific map creation, replacement, expansion and prompt previews without changing the map builder's other lore sources or global templates. Update both the Engine and World Maps to use this setting.

- When the Game Master moves the party to a place more than one step away on the map, such as a boat to the next town, the map now follows by the shortest route instead of staying put. Before, only a move to a place one step away (a place inside, the place around it, or a linked place) moved the map.

- World Maps now uses Marinara Engine's own chat state, notifications and libraries instead of carrying copies of them. A pending map move you cleared no longer comes back, and its notifications appear where you put yours. The download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1487)
- The description now says what it does in plain words.

- Maps can now hold up to 5,000 locations instead of 500, so a whole world fits with its buildings, floors and rooms. Game Mode uses these larger maps on Marinara Engine versions that include the matching update; older versions skip a map over 500 locations when a game starts.
- Child-location maps now use the same square canvas in the editor and runtime, keeping square artwork aligned with the 100×100 coordinate grid. The background picker includes image size guidance.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.
- Track established item descriptions and storage locations on compatible Engines, preserving unchanged details and locked values.
- On compatible Engines, report only changed or removed tracker values while preserving unchanged state and locked rows. Older Engines retain the full-output format.

- The memory page now uses the same header as every other agent page: store banner, logo, name, the Active switch for the open chat and Manage package. Add memories and the setup guide stay in that header. This needs a Marinara version with Capability API 1.390; on older versions nothing changes.

- Other packages can no longer read Long-Term Memory's internal runtime service, which only Marinara itself uses. This needs a Marinara version with Capability API 1.388; on older versions nothing changes. Recall for Slurp and Noodle is unaffected.
- Review: a later chat piece's thread and relationship updates apply together with the rest of the draft instead of one at a time.

- Settings → Extraction adds Hide imported messages from the AI, off by default. Once a Chat Messages piece is imported and extracted, its messages stop being sent to the AI, like the chat summary's Hide summarised messages, so a long chat no longer sends the same history twice. The chat's last messages stay visible, as many as its summary keeps. Turning it off, or permanently deleting a piece's source note, shows exactly the messages it hid; messages you show or hide by hand stay as you set them. A branch made while it is on keeps its copies hidden; show those by hand. It needs a Marinara version that lets packages hide chat messages, and the package now asks for the chat-write permission.

- Settings → Extraction adds Chat import detail. Detailed imports a chat's messages in pieces half the size (12,000 characters instead of 24,000), giving finer memories for about twice the extraction cost. It applies to chats imported from now on; a chat already imported keeps its size.

- When a chat calls one of Long-Term Memory's own characters by part of their name ("Preston" for "Preston Farraday", or the other way round), the memory joins that character's note instead of starting a second one. If the name fits more than one character, it waits for you in review.
- Sources → Chat Summaries keeps the range visible when a chat has a long name: the name is cut, and the message range, day, week or game session stays whole beside it.

- A memory whose score (salience or confidence) the model writes in quotes ("0.5") is kept instead of dropped, and a chat piece whose every memory is malformed fails with Retry instead of reporting success with nothing kept.
- Long-Term Memory no longer offers the older way other Agents read memories. Slurp 0.4.8 and earlier stop adding memories to Creator posts; update Slurp to keep them.

- After you turn on "Other Agents can read memories" and save, Memory Settings offers to turn on Slurp's "What your other Agents know" switch too, since Slurp's Creators need both before they use memories.
- Other Agents that read memories, such as Slurp and Noodle, can ask for whole memories instead of the parts that fit what they are writing. The same memories are shared either way.

- Memory Settings → Recall → Sharing lists each Agent that has read memories with when it last did, how many times it read this week and how many memories it got, so you can tell whether an Agent such as Slurp is using them. The counts come from the Debug activity log, so clearing it or a very busy install can lower them.

- In Sources → Chat Messages, a row with a long chat name cuts the name and keeps the message range visible, so pieces of one chat can be told apart. The range label is also translated (English and Korean).

- A long chat imported from Chat Messages is read in order, one piece after another. From the second piece on, the model sees the end of the piece before it, that piece's events and its open threads, so a memory can say what caused an event or continue a thread across the cut. Different chats still import side by side.

- Re-extract says why it is waiting while settings load, and Run maintenance keeps your place after it finishes.
- Loading placeholders stop pulsing when reduced motion is on, source tool results are announced to screen readers, and a save waiting on recall no longer ends in a stray colon.

- Long-Term Memory now has a Korean interface. It follows the Engine's language setting and shows English for any text without a Korean version. The translation is machine-made and awaits review by a Korean speaker.

- The Chat Messages tab in Sources has a Branch menu for a chat with branches. It starts on this branch, so another branch's messages no longer mix into the list. Choose a branch or All branches; importing still goes to the whole chat.
- Sources lists imported memories whose character, lorebook entry, chat summary or chat message was deleted under "Source gone", so you can remove them with their source or leave them as they are.

- Sources has a Chat Messages tab that learns from a chat's own messages, so a chat without summaries can have memories too. It warns when the chat also has summaries, because importing both can repeat memories in review.
- Whispers, and messages hidden from the AI or from some characters, are left out of chat messages, because a memory can reach every character.
- Needs Marinara Engine 2.5.1 with capability API 1.387, which no longer runs its own memory recall in chats where Long-Term Memory is on.
- Chats with Long-Term Memory on and nothing imported in Sources have no memories on that Engine. Import their messages or summaries from Sources.
- If you used the Engine's old built-in memory, switch Long-Term Memory on in each chat's settings; the package no longer turns it on for those chats.
- The package no longer asks to change chat settings.

- Maintenance, Debug, setup and Chat Settings buttons keep keyboard focus while their work runs, so the result appears where you are.
- Vault and Review controls stay reachable while they save or while identity edits are unsaved, and say why they are locked.
- Sources re-extract and re-import buttons stay reachable during a run and explain why they are waiting.
- Debug, Maintenance and source results are announced to screen readers, and Add section explains why a name was not accepted.
- The setup guide picture and detail header follow the panel's width, and navigation and availability tabs are easier to tap.
- Loading spinners stop spinning when reduced motion is on, and typing in Debug search stays smooth on long logs.

Memory Nag now uses Marinara Engine's own libraries and data cache for its screens instead of carrying copies of them, so the download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1487)

Scans now read Roleplay whispers the way the Engine's own agents do, marked private with who they were for, so a promise made in a whisper can become a memory. A message that is only a whisper is no longer read as empty. This needs a Marinara Engine that shares whispers with Agents; older versions keep reading public messages only.
The description now says what it does in plain words.

Automatic scans wait while a manual message-range scan is active, avoiding duplicate model charges between batches. Finished, stopped, failed, and abandoned scans release the guard without losing checkpoint progress.
Send the saved admin secret on plain-HTTP remote clients too, matching the Engine, so Create Memories no longer fails with an X-Admin-Secret error on LAN and Termux setups.

Choose all unprocessed messages or a specific message range when creating vault memories, so long chats can skip stale history. Closing the progress or prompt window keeps the underlying chat settings open.

- If someone is throwing a party or going to one, they won't make plans with you for those hours, even if you said you can't come. When you invite someone out, you can see the hours they have a party.
- If someone starts dating you knowing you already have a partner, they're okay with it. This also fixes the lives you're already playing.
- On a phone, you can drag the phone button with your finger.
- When a new season starts, people keep last season's outfit until the new one is ready.
- Fixes in the optional Adult Module.

- NPCs is a rule now, life by life: people who aren't in your cast, like a club's staff and its regulars. It's off by default in a new life; a life that already had them keeps it on. Off, they step aside with their pictures, nothing deleted.
- Once you're dating, you can stay the night at theirs, or have them stay at yours.
- No more getting stuck at the end of someone's party, after a lunch break that already went by, with a money request in the middle of an outing, or after reloading during a honeymoon night.
- In the optional Adult Module, the club's dancers and regulars are options that need NPCs.

- Cooking and food: a kitchen at home, twelve recipes, a Cooking skill, and dinner on a date at your place.
- A home of your own: Hillcrest on the hill, buying or a mortgage, furniture for each home, and people noticing where you live.
- People drop by, and you throw parties at home, lived room by room; friends throw theirs, and birthdays are parties now.
- Friends and family can live with you, as many as your home has rooms for.
- Anyone in the cast can be your family, partner, ex or rival from day one.
- Scenes do what's said: favours where they're told, money asked in your own words, outings that follow the talk, a memory for everyone there.
- Clearer Special Actions, work from home, half the practice for skills, and always a way on when the model can't answer.
- Many fixes, and more in the optional Adult Module.

- Contacts no longer freezes: opening it doesn't load your whole life again, and each part of someone's sheet is drawn on its own, so one that can't be shown is just missing and the rest is there.
- If a whole screen can't be shown, it says so, with a button to go back to the map, instead of leaving the game stuck.

- You can use your own pictures for what people wear each season or at work, and for you in any of your outfits: pick one and frame it yourself. Yours stays until you ask for a drawn one again.
- You can rename someone in Settings, and updating from their card brings a new name from the card too.
- When a model puts quotes in the wrong place or leaves part of a line out, the game still reads its reply, so turns in scenes aren't lost.
- The names on the clothes store's rack are sharp again. The phone's shop opens on its own inside a store, and going back returns you to the store with your cart.
- A fix in the optional Adult Module.

- People look like themselves in their pictures: their name, and whether they're a woman or a man, now go with every picture of them, so a character from a series looks like the one you know.
- You can choose how big pictures of one person are drawn, in Settings, right below the size of the other pictures.
- This season's new clothes are for who you play. A character who got dresses they'd never wear gets the season's clothes picked again.
- In the shops, only the things for sale move when you scroll. Eating from your backpack shows up on top of it. The clothes store shows the store behind the clothes again.
- The game finds Marinara however you run it, even from another device or on a secure connection.

- Models that think before they answer, like GLM or DeepSeek, no longer get cut off halfway: every call leaves them room to think, and one that still runs out gets a second try with more room.
- Reasoning has a new option, none, for models that can answer without thinking first.
- Pictures no longer flicker or load again while others are being painted, in Settings and on every other screen.
- Text on the phone, in the Guide and in What's New is sharp again.

- It looks more like a game: a new title screen, a welcome, a first-day card, the GUIDE (a searchable how-it-works app on your phone), a relationship chart in Contacts, and a redone profile.
- Everyone gets their own personality, read from their card, instead of twelve fixed types.
- Relationships go all the way: dating, moving in, engagement and weddings (with more than one partner if all agree), jealousy, open relationships and breakups, each in a scene.
- The town talks: people notice what you do, NEWS every Monday, and friends have opinions.
- Outings are one long scene; plans go on a calendar; birthdays.
- You start without a job: find one in JOBS, interview, get promoted.
- Money: BILLS, debt and eviction; HOMES to move. Five districts, and a motorbike or a car.
- Pictures of key moments, outfits by season, and manual or automatic pictures per life.
- Modules: optional extras you switch on for each life.

- First release, staging only: a modern life sim in its own Home tab.
- A town on a clock with places, opening hours, day and night, and four seasons of thirty days.
- A job, rent, needs and skills; a home with furniture, cooking and a closet; shops, a mall and online orders.
- A cast from your character cards: their weeks, archetypes and gift tastes read by the model, three bonds each, tier events, relationship steps and memories.
- Scenes told by a visual-novel narrator; sleep, knocking on doors and things to do together.
- Alpha: a save from before a change it depends on warns when opened.

- The "Long-Term Memory isn't sharing memories" line now clears as soon as sharing is turned back on.
- Turning on "Use memories from Long-Term Memory" now offers to turn on Long-Term Memory's sharing when it is off.

- New, off by default: Advanced → "Use memories from Long-Term Memory". Posts can draw on what Long-Term Memory remembers about each account's character, as whole memories or only the parts that fit the posts. Turning it on asks first, and a note appears if Long-Term Memory isn't installed or isn't sharing memories.

- Posts, replies, and expanded prompt editors keep the text you are typing visible above the mobile landscape keyboard. Noodle hides its mobile navigation while the keyboard is open and restores it when you finish typing.
- Image failures marked nonretryable by the Engine no longer start automatic replacement requests.
- The sticker, emoji, picture and poll menus now open inside Noodle. That hides the chat emoji-selection settings, which 1.5.7 meant to hide but still showed, and the menus are no longer see-through.

- Noodle now uses Marinara Engine's own settings, dialogs, notifications, Local Model and connection queue instead of carrying copies of them. It no longer resets your Engine settings or starts a second Local Model, its background refreshes wait while a chat on the same connection is replying, and its notifications appear where you put yours. The download is smaller. It needs a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0. On 2.5.0 and older, the version you already have keeps working. (#1478, #1487)
- The sticker and emoji pickers no longer show the chat emoji-selection settings. Those belong to a chat, and Noodle has none.

- With a Claude (Subscription) connection, Noodle no longer makes a hidden second request to name each session, and a request now stops with an error if Claude Code turns on claude.ai connectors. With a Marinara Engine release after 2.5.0, Claude Code also no longer adds your account email, the date or this computer's details to the prompt. Engine 2.5.0's Claude Code still adds them, and the server log warns about it until you update Marinara. (#1313)

- Each character can now use their own image generation connection for Noodle images. Open the character's Noodle profile, choose Edit profile and pick it under Image connection. The choice saves right away. Use Noodle image connection keeps the connection from Noodle's settings. Noodle still needs an image connection in its settings or a default image connection before it makes images.

- The switch that adds a character's image instructions to their Noodle images is now in Noodle. Open the character's Noodle profile, choose Edit profile and find it under the profile fields. Edit image instructions opens the character's Convo tab, where you write the instructions. Your current choice carries over. The link needs Marinara Engine with capability API 1.67; on an older Engine, the switch works without the link.

- Interpret image prompts now works without an Agents default connection. When none is set under Settings → Connections → Defaults, Noodle's own text connection rewrites the image prompt. Before, the rewrite was skipped, so your image connection's Image Prompting Instructions had no effect and the style profile's Style text was pasted into the prompt.
- Include descriptions now gives the character's appearance notes to the AI that rewrites the image prompt instead of leaving them in the prompt it edits, where they reached ComfyUI as plain text. With Interpret image prompts off, the notes are still added as written.
- Style text you write into Auto or a copy of it now guides the rewrite too.
- If the rewrite copies a full sentence of your Image Prompting Instructions, the Style text or the character's image habits, Noodle removes it. Short phrases and tag lists such as "masterpiece, best quality" stay.
- The help texts now say what happens when Interpret image prompts is off.

- Image prompts no longer include text meant for the AI that writes them. The poster's Personality and image habits and your image connection's Image Prompting Instructions now only guide the rewrite that Interpret image prompts runs. Before, Noodle pasted them word for word into the prompt sent to ComfyUI and other image services, which broke tag-only prompts. With Interpret image prompts off, or when the rewrite fails, the image service gets the prompt without them.
- A style profile's Style text now reaches the rewrite once, as guidance, instead of also sitting in the prompt it edits. The Auto profile's note "Infer a consistent visual style from the character, game, scene, and selected image model" never ends up in the image prompt. Style text from the other profiles still applies when no rewrite runs.

- New Show images to the writer switch in Settings → Advanced → Image Understanding. Turn it off and Noodle never sends timeline images to the model that writes your timeline. Image captioning, when on, still sends them to the captioning connection, which is the Noodle generation connection unless you choose another. The switch is on by default, so nothing changes unless you turn it off.
- The Image captioning help now says what happens when it is off: the writer model gets up to 8 recent timeline images, if Show images to the writer is on and the model accepts them.

- Noodle can now translate posts and comments for you. Turn on Translate posts automatically in Settings → General. It uses the translator defaults you saved in a chat's Translation settings and leaves what your personas wrote alone. Posts already in your language get no extra copy, and turning the switch off stops the translations still waiting.
- Translations now stay after you refresh the timeline, leave Noodle or reload the page, and a translation you hide stays hidden. This browser keeps them, so another device translates again.

- Fixed timeline refreshes on local models that failed after a short, empty-looking answer. When the prompt plus the room Noodle keeps for its answer did not fit the connection's context window, Noodle cut your characters, chats and timeline out of the prompt before sending. It now keeps the whole prompt and lowers the answer limit instead. If too little room is left for an answer, the refresh stops and says what to turn down.

- You can now translate posts and comments, your own included. Pick Translate in a post's menu or under a comment, and use the same button to hide it again. Noodle uses the translator defaults you saved in a chat's Translation settings, or Google Translate into English if you have not saved any.
- In Chrome on Android, adding a picture to a post or comment now offers the camera as well as your files. The Marinara Android app doesn't offer the camera yet.
- Noodle's description now says what it is in plain words.
- When Noodle cannot load, it now says so instead of showing an empty timeline. If Marinara Engine blocked it because this device has no Admin Secret, it explains how to set one.
- Widgets on Homescreen now available.
- Search icons and post menus keep Noodle's selected accent when Engine Chroma animates.

- Applying a saved prompt asks before replacing the current prompt, including edits already saved as the active prompt.
- Cancel works immediately in Delete All Noodle Data; only deletion requires typing DELETE.
- A running timeline refresh blocks duplicate refresh requests instead of queuing extra generations.
- GLM 5.3 on NanoGPT and Z.AI keeps its required reasoning enabled when the selected effort is None.
- Maintenance: simplify the inline composer's visibility checks and remove unused code.
- After a love interest's finale, the story no longer assumes they already confessed: if you eased off before the words came, they can still say it later.

- **Banned phrases** in Settings → Content: type the words and phrases you never want to read, separated by commas or one per line, and every scene, message and note avoids them.
- Love interests no longer stop an intimate scene to check in or offer to stop, sex included. Ease off is still yours.
- Your protagonist takes a moment to sit with what matters to them, a first kiss, a night together, a quarrel, a secret learned, in thoughts in their own voice, with their doubts and hopes showing, before the story moves on.
- **Slow burn:** through a love interest's first two stages, neither of you says what you feel. From the third stage they may confess once the story has earned it, and by their route's finale at the latest. Desire can still come first, as your Heat allows.
- Under NSFW: Explicit, sex scenes are no longer rushed: they take the room they need, from the build-up to the aftermath, with the characters talking, asking for what they want and saying what they feel along the way.

- Each love interest has their own Claw Machine plush: the animal that fits them best, in their colours (a cyan raven with red eyes, a black cat with violet eyes). Your Planning model draws it once, in the background, the first time you open Dates. Until then their plush wears their look, as before.

- Your protagonist knows only what the story has shown them: love interests no longer talk as if you already know their past, their habits or the words of their world, and a newcomer learns this world as they go.
- A story set in an existing world, such as Teyvat from Genshin Impact, stays that world and keeps its canon.
- Chapters make room for other people, scenes without a love interest, and rest or sleep after a long day.

- Memories banners follow your Heat: under NSFW: Fade their Memories and Moments mix SFW and suggestive situations, and under NSFW: Explicit explicit ones too. Snapshots stay SFW.
- An explicit Memory's art can now be explicit under NSFW: Explicit with the Explicit image rating. Lower either setting before it's painted, and it shows the same moment clothed. Other Memory art stays clothed, as before.

- Chapters no longer all end the same way. Each one builds differently, and its closing choice is a different kind of decision from the last few, not a love interest stepping in again to ask whom you'll go with. A rival love interest competes over more than just you, too.

- **Read Me**, a new game in Dates: a love interest studies you and makes four guesses about you. Answer Spot on, Close or Not at all, and tell them the truth in your own words if you like.
- They remember: each answer goes into their notebook of what they know about you (likes, dislikes, habits, fears, dreams), and they bring it up in scenes, Home notes, messages and dates. No other love interest ever sees it.
- Open the notebook from Read Me to read it, rewrite your words or delete an entry. A delete is final.

- The Love Timeline shows every 4★ Moment and 5★ Memory you've won, on the day you won it, including ones won before this update. Each Snapshot, Moment and Memory says what it is and opens in the Album.

- The story's **Image description** shows only for a picture that isn't on screen: a painted background or key image no longer has its description under the chapter title, and one whose file fails to load gets it back.
- NSFW stories now say outright that crude and vulgar words, swearing and dirty talk included, are fine wherever they fit a character's voice. In SFW stories characters may swear too, without the sexual words.
- A 5★ reveal with a long premise fits on a phone: the card never grows past the screen, so the title shows whole and the premise scrolls inside it.

- **The Closer:** a main chapter can now end on a warm climax instead of a Confrontation. Over three rounds the love interest offers something of themselves, and you answer: **Reassure**, **Tease**, **Mirror** (share something of your own) or **Ask**.
- It ends **Opened up** (trust grows, and it's a first on your Love Timeline), **Almost** (nothing changes) or **Shut out** if it goes wrong (trust falls, and they hold it against you).
- In NSFW stories, Opened up can turn intimate, drawing on their tastes and your role.
- After two main chapters end the same way, the next ends with the other, so a story in progress gets its first Closer soon. Route chapters keep their Confrontations.

- NSFW stories give each new love interest's bible their tastes in sex and intimacy: what they're into, kinks included, and what draws them. Intimate scenes bring them in when they fit; your content settings still decide what a scene may hold.
- An older cast gets **Add intimacy preferences** on Your cast (1 call). Read and edit them in the bible.
- An optional Sub, Dom or Switch preference for your protagonist sits beside Heat.
- SFW stories never write or send any of it.
- Story memory keeps an NSFW story as it was written: summaries no longer turn it SFW, and a Veil is remembered as having happened off the page.
- The planners no longer call every love interest a monster: each is a human, even if inside a monster.
- A date inside a chapter can go as hoped: it stumbles only when the story gives it a reason, like Date Night.

- In stories, hide the header's Image description panel while a character sprite is shown; keep the description available without a sprite.
- Four-star memories include artwork through the existing painting flow alongside their playable memory.
- Round every corner of story character nameplates.
- Make desktop fullscreen fill the available Otome Hearth area across its screens. Leaving fullscreen restores ordinary portrait layouts while preserving drafts and the current reader line.

- Restore the scrolling mobile Settings category strip, and keep each cast member's repaint actions together.
- Show progress toward the next Affection level in Between you.
- Facial expression edits use an adult, nonsexual face-edit policy while preserving the current look, clothing and style. Non-explicit Suggestive images keep concise content exclusions without unrelated graphic boilerplate.
- Edit a love interest’s image appearance above their spoiler Bible without repainting or changing their story.
- Choose an existing Assets Music folder in Audio settings when music generation is off.
- Give chapters and scenes room for ordinary moments, earned emotional payoffs, and character change.

- Read a love interest’s intended appearance from Your cast or Who’s home without opening Bible spoilers. Wardrobe looks and reached story illustrations also expose their existing visual descriptions, including when no image was painted.
- After adding an image connection, missing story locations and key moments offer the existing explicit Paint action with its image cost and prompt review. Reading descriptions and saving image settings paint nothing.

- Automatically painted current-location backgrounds prepare before reading begins, with the existing manual-paint and failure paths retained.
- Story generation can reuse saved location artwork for recurring settings instead of painting a new numbered visit.
- Protagonist dialogue, thoughts and performed choices explicitly follow the selected persona’s authored identity and the player’s writing instructions.

- Opening narration no longer previews the portrait of a love interest whose speaking turn has not been reached. Established speakers can still stay visible during later narration.

- The pre-chapter warning places its Ease off feather after the guidance sentence.

- Harmful story/date choices and Confrontation outcomes can reduce Affection progress within the current level. Unlocked levels stay permanent, and replaying never repeats the deduction or refunds daily earning limits.

- Album Memories can be filtered by 3★, 4★ or 5★, with unplayed content listed first.

- Owned 3★ Snapshots can be illustrated on first opening through the existing image connection, confirmation and prompt review flow. Paintings are saved and reused; old vignettes and story progress stay intact.

- Suggestive is an image-content ceiling: neutral portraits and facial expression edits no longer receive mandatory suggestive or sensitive-content tags. Image briefs follow the actual moment, with non-explicit adult intimacy allowed when appropriate.
- Wish and Wardrobe display cleaned love-interest and persona outfits while retaining the original paintings. Wardrobe banner art is centered and shown whole, and tapping a ready banner image opens a full-image view without making a wish.

- Desktop settings use the available stage space, with every settings section reachable and long pages scrollable.
- Text generation can recover when an endpoint rejects the optional JSON-format hint, while retaining reply validation and output budgets.

- Attempted fix for item images going missing. An uploaded or generated image now stays with its
  item, even after a rename. Images uploaded before this update are kept on rename too.
- A dropped connection no longer hides item images until you reload.
- Item editor: a line under the name shows which image file the item uses. Unlink sends this
  chat's item back to matching by name without deleting the file.
- Bag cards have an [i] on the image with the same details. Deleting an image file moved to the
  × in the item editor, which says the file is shared by every chat and offers Unlink instead.
- A new image never replaces another item's file: it's saved as "apple (1).png" and so on.
- Item names with characters like "/" upload correctly.
- No changes you'll notice: a code comment was corrected.

- Accepting or keeping a pending item change and then switching chats before it finishes no
  longer shows that chat's result in the chat you switched to.
- The "Only you can change it — becomes shown" help now says removals are skipped too.

- Hide items and outfits from their ⋯ menu. Hidden ones get their own Bag tab and are kept from
  the agent: it only sees a hidden item while you're wearing it.
- New Hidden Items settings choose what the agent may do to a hidden item, and whether it asks
  first. Asking shows the change side by side so you can accept it or keep the old details.
- Lock an item's description from the item editor so the agent can't change it.
- Feed appearance has seven options, including equipped item names and descriptions. Outfit
  portraits follow the same setting.
- Build Wardrobe can use hidden items when you allow it, and always asks you about each one first.
- Optional Delete button on item and outfit cards (Settings → Display, saved per device).
- Re-equipping an outfit whose item was deleted now brings the item back with its default slot.

- Build Wardrobe layers clothing properly: when two pieces of an outfit share a layer (tights and a
  skirt over them), the outer one moves up a layer instead of being left out.
- New artwork for the clothing layers, socks and Extra Wearable slots; the inner torso and legs
  icons are now a shirt and leggings.

- Clothing layers on the portrait ring are now a stack of cards, so the dock stays about as wide as
  before. Use the arrows on the card or tap a layer's tab to switch; worn layers keep their
  highlighted outline.

- Layered clothing: torso and legs each have Inner, Mid and Outer clothing slots, so a shirt,
  waistcoat and jacket (or tights under shorts) can be worn together. Existing clothing becomes the
  Inner layer.
- New Socks slot, plus three Extra Wearable slots for anything no other slot fits.
- The tracker agent and Build Wardrobe use the new slots. If you customized the tracker prompt,
  reset it to the default to pick them up.

- With an Admin Secret saved, each image now loads once and is reused, instead of reloading after
  every change in the dock.
- An image that failed to load for a reason other than having no image tries again when the dock is
  reopened, and changing the saved Admin Secret retries every image.

- Works from other devices and remote access: Quartermaster now sends the Admin Secret saved in
  Settings → Advanced → Admin Access, fixing "Invalid or missing X-Admin-Secret header".
- Item images, outfit portraits and slot icons also load from other devices.
- A missing or mismatched Admin Secret now explains how to fix it.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.

- Image uploads and outfit saves report their own result when other edits finish at the same time.
- A completed upload cannot close a newer dialog or show its error in another chat.
- Late inventory refreshes no longer undo a completed edit or replace a newer refresh.

- Detached tracker elements wait until mounted before starting subscriptions or changing the active chat.
- Late image-connection checks and failed mutations no longer overwrite another dialog or chat's state.
- Failed image deletions preserve the image even when another request finishes at the same time.
- Closing the active chat clears its old error from the tracker panel.

- Rebuilding the dock now closes its dialogs and clears their pending sessions.
- A late wardrobe confirmation cannot replace a newly opened dialog or another chat's view.

- Available from the official staging Download Agents catalog with Professor Mari's armored
  Quartermaster cover and installation guidance.
- Closing the dock also closes its dialogs; an old image-prompt preview cannot replace a later
  dialog or another chat's preview. Failed inventory exports now report their error.
- A failed outfit save cannot overwrite an existing outfit's portrait.

- Fixed the Settings avatar-swap toggle showing a stale value from the previous chat after a
  failed reload.
- Fixed a failed image delete permanently hiding an item's picture instead of just the delete.
- Fixed the Build Wardrobe and Generate Image modals letting a stale, still-running generation
  overwrite what a later session in the same modal was showing.
- Fixed the tracker panel briefly reappearing over the toolbar button in a rare mount-reuse case.
- Corrected the README's stated minimum Engine version to 2.4.6, matching the manifest.

- Raised the minimum required Engine version to 2.4.6, matching what this has actually been
  tested against recently.

- Brief toast notifications now appear when the tracker agent adds, updates, equips, or removes
  an item -- visible even with the dock closed.
- Items can now be favorited with a star, which sorts them to the top of the Bag.

- Fixed the Recent Agent Update box leak for real this time — 0.1.13 and 0.1.14 were both
  attempted fixes that didn't fully resolve it.
- Widened the info tooltip box so long macro tokens read on one line.

- Attempted fix for the Recent Agent Update collapsed-box leak (0.1.13's attempt didn't fully
  resolve it either).
- Fixed tooltip text overflowing outside its own box.

- Attempted fix for Recent Agent Update's collapsed box showing a sliver of Restore Inventory
  underneath.
- Info tooltips and card overflow menus no longer clip against the dock's edge.
- Shrank the item card's quantity field to match the "⋯" button beside it.
- "+ Add Item" is now green, matching Save Current Outfit.

- The Relationship Tracker button now opens its relationship web on phones. Close the sheet with its close button, Escape, or a tap outside; focus returns to the button. Changing chats or removing the tracker closes the old sheet.
- Desktop keeps its existing Trackers drawer and passive preview. Opening the web reads saved relationships without running a model.

- Korean, Japanese and Chinese now work. A name followed directly by a Korean particle (김민수는) or written without spaces in Japanese (アリスは) or Chinese (张三很信任李四) now counts as naming that character. Before, Update from History and automatic updates rejected these sentences, and Scene-only couldn't tell who was present.
- A longer card name doesn't count as a shorter one: 김민수 isn't 김민, and アリス isn't リス. Single characters and syllables appear inside ordinary words, so a one-character Chinese or Japanese name still needs a space or punctuation next to it, and a one-syllable Korean name counts only before a particle (준은, but not 준비).
- When a persona perception is rejected, the message now says which name it expected.

- When Update from History can't use the model's answer, it now shows the changes the model suggested instead of only an error. Each change uses character names, says in plain words what needs fixing, and can be edited, removed or saved. Relationship changes and persona perceptions are saved separately, and the model's original answer is under Details for bug reports.
- Fewer "unknown character alias" errors: the tracker now tells the model to keep your persona out of character pairs, and a pair it still files with your persona is offered as that character's view of you. The error now names the alias the model used.
- Update from History no longer fails when the model leaves out an empty list.
- After saving only persona perceptions, the panel says how many it saved.

- In Roleplay, Update from History now reads whispers the way the Engine's own agents do, marked private with who they were for. A message that is only a whisper is no longer read as empty.
- This needs a Marinara Engine that shares whispers with Agents. On older versions, the tracker keeps reading public messages only.

- Fixed Update from History failing with "Persona update 1 must contain exactly five values" when a persona is active. The tracker now tells the model the exact shape of a persona perception, so it stops copying the lock flag into its answer.
- The same fix helps automatic updates, which were quietly skipping those persona perception changes.
- If a model still returns the wrong shape, the error now says how many values it sent.

- In the Tracker Panel, Relationship Tracker now has the same collapsible header as World, Persona and the other trackers instead of its own card, and remembers whether you collapsed it. While it runs, the header shows a small spinner.
- In the desktop Trackers window, the drawer's own header is used, and Relationship Tracker's button now matches the other trackers' buttons.

- Fixed "Invalid or missing X-Admin-Secret header" when Marinara is opened from another device (LAN, phone, or proxy). The panel now sends the admin secret saved on that device and explains where to save it.
- Update from History falls back to the default agent connection, then the chat's, when no tracker connection is chosen.
- Automatic runs keep valid changes when the model omits an empty list or returns one malformed persona entry.
- Switching persona or removing a card mid-run no longer reports a failed run.
- Tapping a line label or finishing an automatic update no longer wipes unsaved editor text or closes open sections.
- The persona no longer covers a lone character or sits under relationship lines, and its arrowheads show.
- The lock checkbox stays beside its label at Compact width; status colours are readable in the light theme.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.

- First staging release, with Professor Mari and Crimson Orc sharing pasta as its catalogue cover. Tracks character-card relationships and each character's one-way perception of the active persona in Roleplay group chats, drawn as a fixed-circle relationship web in the Tracker Panel.
- Conservative automatic tracking after each completed reply, a bounded Update from History (1-100 messages), manual editing, optional per-line locks, and Resume Automatic.
- Two prompt-injection modes: All relationships, or Scene-only relationships. Presence lookback (default 15 messages) decides Scene-only eligibility; the automatic tracker's Context Size (default 5) is separate.
- Touch and pen: press a relationship line to reveal its label and press elsewhere to dismiss it; desktop keeps hover and keyboard-focus labels.
- Read-only API for other packages: GET /api/relationship-tracker/v1/chats/:chatId/relationships.
- The description now says what it does in plain words.

- Shield, Uncanny Dodge and Counterspell work. When a blow hits you, the fight asks whether you cast Shield (the same roll is checked again against your new Armor Class) or take Uncanny Dodge (its damage is halved). When somebody casts a spell, it asks whether you counter it.
- Six SRD monsters Parry, and spellcasting monsters such as the Mage can cast Shield and Counterspell back.
- You can grapple and shove, and break free of a grapple.
- Bless, Bane, Shield of Faith, Haste, Slow, Blur, Faerie Fire, Guiding Bolt, Vicious Mockery, Longstrider and Ray of Frost change the numbers they print.
- Exhaustion levels 1, 2, 3 and 5 count in a fight. A poisoned fighter, or a frightened one while it can see what frightens it, rolls its side of a grapple or shove at disadvantage.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.46.

- Eleven SRD spellcasters now cast in a fight, off their own sheet and spell slots, at the numbers their stat block prints: the Acolyte, Priest, Cult Fanatic, Druid, Mage, Archmage, Lich, Mummy Lord, both nagas and the Androsphinx. The Gynosphinx prepares nothing a fight can use, so it still fights with its claws.
- Hellish Rebuke works: when something damages you, the fight asks whether you cast it back at them.
- Sacred Flame, Acid Splash, Poison Spray, Vicious Mockery and Spiritual Weapon now deal damage. Before, a fight never offered them.
- Two new sheet fields, Spell attack: other bonus and Spell save DC: other bonus.
- Counterspell, Shield and Feather Fall still stay off the menu, and the README says why.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.34.

- Extra Attack works. Set Attacks per Attack action on your sheet and one Attack buys that many strikes: the first spends the action and the rest are free. A crossbow still fires once, because it loads.
- Sneak Attack is a rider your rogue simply has: hit with a finesse or ranged weapon while you have advantage, or while another enemy stands beside your target. It grows with the Rogue table, 1d6 to 10d6.
- Action Surge hands you a second action and costs nothing. Cunning Action puts Dash, Disengage and Hide on your menu for a bonus action.
- Dodge now also gives advantage on Dexterity saves. Charmed stops you turning on the charmer and lifts if they go down, frightened stops you walking closer, restrained hampers Dexterity saves, and petrified halves all damage.
- A monster's blow carries its second damage clause, so a dragon's bite burns again.
- Weapon rows you already picked know none of the new columns. Pick them again, or tick the boxes.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.32.

- A battle can be fought on a board in feet. Set the game's combat style to Tactical and your Speed becomes squares you walk between attacks. Classic plays the same fight flat.
- Weapons know how far they reach: a longsword strikes the next square, a glaive two, and a bow carries to its long range with disadvantage.
- Shooting with an enemy beside you is also rolled with disadvantage, and a target in trees or ruins is 2 harder to hit.
- Spells and breath weapons land as the shapes the SRD prints: Fireball a burst, a dragon's breath a real cone. Everybody in it is caught, friends too.
- Walk out of an ogre's reach and it swings at you, spending its reaction. Disengage first and it does not.
- Weapon rows you already picked have none of the new distances. Delete each one and pick it again, or an old bow only fires at somebody beside you.
- Still to come: choosing whether to strike at a walker, three-quarters cover, elevation, grapple and shove.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.28.

- Battles in a new game on this ruleset are now fought with 5e rules, on screen: the d20 attack roll with advantage, a natural 20 that hits and doubles the damage dice, a natural 1 that misses, your weapons and prepared spells, the SRD conditions, concentration, death saves and spell slots spent off your sheet.
- Adds a bestiary: 319 SRD monsters with their armour class, hit dice, saves, resistances, immunities, attacks, breath weapons, multiattacks and legendary actions, every number taken from the printed stat block.
- A challenge-rating scale measured from those monsters, so an opponent a Game Master invents can be pulled onto it.
- Cantrip damage now grows with your level, Magic Missile is three darts that simply hit, and fifteen well-known spells say which condition they apply.
- Second Wind is spent as a bonus action, which is what the SRD says.
- Not yet: positions and movement, reactions, and the window a legendary action is spent in.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.27.

- Class resources you pick now keep themselves. Rage, Ki, Sorcery Points, Channel Divinity, Action Surge and Indomitable follow their class tables, Bardic Inspiration and Divine Sense follow your Charisma, and the sheet sets the maximum and keeps it current as you level up.
- Lay on Hands is a new class resource. Its pool is your level times 5.
- A kept maximum is shown as read only on the sheet. If you want your own number, delete the picked row and type one: a row you typed is never kept by the ruleset.
- Your sheet has one Level field, so a multiclass character's class resources follow the total level.
- Rage stops at six. The Barbarian table says Unlimited at 20th level, which a counter cannot hold.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.23.

- Battles now start from your character sheet. Your hit points and spell slots go into the fight, and when it ends the damage you took and the slots you spent are written back. Pact Magic slots do not transfer: their level follows the character, which the battle block cannot say yet.
- Your prepared spells and the weapons you picked from the catalogs show up as skills. Cantrips come too, because they are cast without being prepared. A row you typed by hand carries no numbers, so it stays out.
- Health is carried as a share of your maximum, so a character at half hit points starts the fight at half of the health bar.
- The damage is still Marinara's own combat math. Attack rolls, saving throws and concentration are not applied, so this is not a 5e combat system.
- SRD healing spells now heal: Cure Wounds, Healing Word, Mass Cure Wounds, Mass Healing Word, Prayer of Healing, Heal, Mass Heal and Regenerate.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.22.

- Adds catalogs: ready-made SRD 5.1 entries the character sheet editor offers in a picker, so you no longer type a spell list or a page of class features row by row. 319 spells, 208 class and subclass features, and 36 weapons.
- Picking a class feature that the SRD gives a plain number of uses, such as Second Wind, Rage or Ki, also fills in the class resource that tracks it.
- A picked row is a copy. Edit it however you like, and nothing rewrites your character later.
- Battles still use Marinara's default combat, so the numbers a catalog entry carries are recorded but not yet rolled.
- Needs an Engine with Capability API 1.21.

- First release. Ships the 5e SRD 5.1 ruleset data for Game Mode ability checks, skill checks, saving throws, spell slots, hit dice, class resources, conditions, rests, and a full character sheet. Battles still use Marinara's default combat, not 5e combat.
- Available to Engine staging users only, and needs an Engine with Capability API 1.20.
- On a wide screen, an open Background, Caretaker, Looks or New egg panel no longer stretches the stage card beside it.
- On a wide screen, Background, Caretaker, Looks and New egg open in their own box under the meters and care buttons, instead of across the bottom of the Nook.

- One new egg a day. Once one has come, the egg button says what time the next one is ready. Eggs found in chat and saucelings brought back from the Menagerie don't count.
- On a phone, Background scrolls into view when it opens, like Caretaker, Looks and New egg, and Escape closes it.

- Background: an error belongs to the last thing you tried and clears once something works. The description box waits while a place is suggested, so it never replaces what you typed.
- Evolve: Keep works while the new looks are still being written; only a choice already sent has to finish.
- After a repaint, your sauceling no longer drops to a silhouette while its new pictures load.
- Settings: a number that fails to save goes back to the saved one, and a picture connection that was deleted shows as missing instead of blank.
- Album: a sauceling brought back from the Menagerie is no longer shown twice.
- Moving the egg no longer closes a rename or a hand-over you were in the middle of.
- Painted sheets with two or three touching rows of drawings are read correctly.
- An egg find that fails (the writing connection does not answer) no longer uses up the day's find.
- Talking with the caretaker counts toward an evolution offer on the day the egg hatches or after a hand-over.

- The Nook's "⋯" button also holds Caretaker, Looks and New egg. Each opens its own panel under the Nook; close it with ✕ or Escape.
- About only describes your sauceling: its look, sauce, traits and who found it.
- The tour card wraps a long caretaker name instead of pushing its buttons off the screen.

- On the large Home widget, the caretaker no longer towers over the card: both figures are sized to the card's width.
- Feed, Play, Rest and Cuddle (or Warm, Talk and Listen for an egg) are behind one "Care" button in the bottom-right corner. Tap it and the buttons open to its left; tap it again, or press Escape, to put them away. The button glows when a care would help.

- The Nook's top bar holds one "⋯" button: Rename, Background and Tour are inside it. "Name it" stays in view until your sauceling has a name.
- Ask is one line until you open it, under Check in.
- When your caretaker has offered an evolution, the reason is written beside the Evolve button instead of behind a "?".
- Settings are grouped under Visits, Writing and Pictures, with shorter notes and a narrower column on a wide screen. On a phone, pickers take the full width instead of being cut off.
- A caretaker with a long name no longer pushes the buttons in About off the edge of a phone screen.
- On a narrow screen, the number boxes in Settings no longer shrink until the value is cut off.

- The Journal says how many entries are new since you last looked.
- A pet whose Journal is empty now says so, instead of saying there is no sauceling.
- The meters in the Nook jump to their new level when reduced effects or reduced motion is on, instead of sliding.
- On the Home widgets, a meter that needs care now shows its amber fill, and the waiting badge on a care button has its colour back.

- The large Nook widget shows the caretaker's latest line under the stage, with the AI label when a model wrote it. The small widget carries the label too.
- The widgets open from a real button, so a keyboard or screen reader can reach them. A resting care button on the large widget says when it's ready again instead of doing nothing.
- Errors, the delete confirmations and the AI label follow your Engine theme's colours, and the Journal uses the same AI label as the rest.

- The Menagerie explains what comes to it, shows a dot on its tab when a character finds an egg, and picks the finder to look after a found egg.
- Lock stage has a help tip. Replaying the tour on a hatched sauceling starts with a step about it.
- The Journal groups lines by day; with no sauceling it offers a button to the Nook.
- The Album says how to paint the first picture and what a keepsake is. Hiding "Add instructions" keeps what you typed.
- Rename is spelled out, the care window setting reads more plainly, and with no characters the Nook says who looks after the egg.
- Saved backgrounds say they're shared by all your saucelings, and their delete button is easier to tap.

- Easier first steps. Mari greets you in an empty nook and gives a short tour after your first egg; the Tour button replays it.
- Tap a meter's name to see what it does. "Growing paused" now shows under Hunger, and an egg says how it hatches.
- A resting care button, and Bring back in the Menagerie, now say why they can't be used yet.
- About is split into Caretaker, Looks and New egg. Retiring and handing over to another caretaker ask first.
- Settings keeps the image options together and shows a Saved tick. Errors read as plain sentences, with the details a tap away.
- The voice offer comes after the egg arrives, and Esc skips it instead of cancelling the egg. Special saucelings fold away until you want them.

- First beta of Saucelings, a pet that lives in Home → Saucelings and on the Home widget grid.
- Pick one of your characters to look after an egg. They care for it on their own schedule and talk in their own voice, drawn from their card, and you cover the gaps they miss.
- How the two of you care for it shapes its temperament. Retire elders to the Menagerie and bring them back whenever you like.
- With your image connection: pixel-art paintings for the Album, a figure of your caretaker for the Nook, and backgrounds of your own.
- Characters you chat with may now and then find an egg of a creature they invent. Not every egg is an ordinary one.
- Install it, restart Marinara Engine when prompted, then open Home → Saucelings.

- Wardrobe import finds looks again. It accepts untidy model replies (other list names, extra fields, long summaries, tags as one line) and has room for long replies and thinking models.
- The "Legacy wardrobe note" source says "(empty)" when the Creator has no old note, so it is clear why you cannot pick it.
- Long-Term Memory no longer turns people from your chats into collabs. Creators keep those people out of posts and DMs unless the brief names them, and new installs recall only the relevant memories.

- Backstage (Engine link) no longer says Long-Term Memory isn't sharing after its "Other Agents can read memories" switch is turned on. The line clears at once after Slurp's offer, and the next time the panel loads after Long-Term Memory's offer or Memory Settings.

- Turning on "What your other Agents know" now asks whether to turn on Long-Term Memory's "Other Agents can read memories" when that switch is off. "Turn it on" changes only that switch; "Not now" leaves it alone.

- Creators' posts and DM replies now use what Long-Term Memory remembers about them, through its recall service. A new "Long-term memory" choice in Backstage (Engine link) sets whether they get whole memories (the default) or only the parts that fit the post or message. It shows while "What your other Agents know" is on.
- Backstage says when Long-Term Memory is missing, or is not sharing ("Other Agents can read memories" is off in its Memory Settings).
- A DM brings in the persona's memories only when that persona's Slurp page uses Linked identity. A hinted or concealed page never does.
- The Creator brief no longer reads Long-Term Memory's storage; the Character Tracker, World State and Persona Stats lines are unchanged.

- World lens: the canon-anchor reading also returns `world` (era, device, money, festivals). Cache version v4 → v5, so each card is read once more in the background. A modern card has no lens and nothing changes.
- The Creator brief (posts, DMs, comment replies, scenes, Stir suggestions, rewritten fan lines) and both live show prompts get one "Your world" line for a non-modern lens. Drama and Support desk prompts do not use the brief and are unchanged.
- Pictures: a non-modern Creator never gets the mirror, desk or screenshot camera source, so no phone or screen appears. The image model gets no world words.
- Holidays: when events run, a non-modern Creator is told to play them as their world's nearest festival.
- Culture-shock fans: about 1 in 4 regular fan comments under a non-modern Creator's post comes from a free bank per era.
- Backstage: the canon-anchor editor shows and edits the world (era, device, money, festivals); a player's fix survives a new reading.

- Fan comments see the post: a short title (40 characters or fewer) gets quoted in some questions and reactions, the question bank has 16 more lines, and a fan line is skipped when the same text is already under the post.
- Fan questions as callbacks: a top-level fan question under the Creator's recent posts (1–30 days old) is a new callback kind, `question`, so a later post may answer it.
- Five business arcs join the built-in arc library: sale week, burnout and comeback, new gear, leak scare and page anniversary. Saved libraries get them through the existing normalize step.

- Niches: the card reading now names each Creator's page niche (main + up to two side niches, from a fixed list). The reading refreshes once for every Creator.
- Post jobs: each ordinary post gets a kind (try-on haul, gym set, finished commission, stream setup, fan request, teaser, …). The niche weighs the jobs, the main niche keeps at most half of the last 8 posts, and a Creator never repeats one of their last 3 jobs. Spice is not changed.
- Card notes edits keep the niche.
- Jobs fit the post: a job with its own place (gym, kitchen, stage) only goes on a post with no place yet, intimate jobs need a card heat of at least flirty, and avoided topics drop the job.
- The card reading refreshes once for every Creator; on a card you never edited, the heat range may shift a little with the new reading.

- Outfits change: a Creator who never had a wardrobe gets one filled from the card once (a closet you emptied stays empty), so pictures stop showing the same clothes.
- Pictures follow your image style: a painted style no longer gets "personal photograph" words. In the story it is still a photo.
- Automatic captions are short lines under the picture (about 40–160 characters, cut at a sentence end above 280).
- Halloween costume contest in October (Settings › Stir › Drama): three Creators post costumes, you pick the winner, the winner posts a reward set.
- Live recaps are built from the show (what you got, goals, coins, top tipper), so two shows never post the same text.
- The daily world tick sees the recent themes, so the feed no longer gets "Cozy" trends day after day.
- Fewer wasted slots: the planner stops adding post slots past posts per day, and one slot opens one campaign.

- Live shows, rebuilt: code runs every show minute by minute (fans, tips, menu orders, goals); while you watch, the model writes the host and the chat, and the host answers you by name.
- Live pictures about once per minute, and private shows at the Backstage price and length.
- Go live yourself as your persona's Creator, or as any Creator from Stir; the room reacts and suggests your next move.
- "X is live" notices, a thank-you post after each show, and a Backstage > Live shows page.
- The cam is told in words on the stage, so a show works without pictures; pictures follow those words. A live Creator's Moments tile opens the show. Live is portrait on every screen, with a slim top bar.

- Slurp starts again on Engine builds with zod 4. The feed post and Creator generation routes no longer stop at load with "Right-hand side of 'instanceof' is not an object" (zod 4 has no `ZodEffects`); they extend the plain object schemas instead.

- Slurp starts again on Engine builds with zod 4. Settings sections with nested defaults are filled in again, so the server no longer stops at load with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'curve')".
- On zod 4 Engines, saving part of the Slurp settings, a Garnish ad or a creator account no longer resets the fields you did not send to their defaults. Creator access and auto-posting defaults are filled in again too.
- Fixed Story viewer clicks passing through to the feed or Engine behind it. Close, Creator profile, menu, navigation and picture controls respond again.

One release for everything built since 0.3.53 (unreleased 0.3.54 to 0.3.65 folded in):

- Storylines: arcs, dramas and situations run on one storyline engine; Story Packs import v2 files, one JSON `fit`, one Packs list with a gate and Remove, topic switches `<pack>:<topic>`.
- Packs (off by default): Family pack and five kink packs (Lingerie, Cosplay, Feet, Dom/sub, Exhibition).
- Intimacy ladder: rapport tiers open doors in DMs (`slurpRapportDoors`), the highest tier is kept.
- Paid sexting sessions (`SlpSextingBar`); Stir as a slide-up sheet (`SlpStirDeck`); Stories in Slurp's own layer.
